definitions.explanation: A native Japanese counter that can be used for various objects, especially when the specific counter is unknown. Only used for numbers 1-9.

examples.japanese: ⟦{一|ひと}→一：noentry⟧つ⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
⟦りんご→りんご：02269_ringo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{三|みっ}→三：noentry⟧つ⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{二|ふた}→二：noentry⟧つ⟦あります→ある：00006_aru⟧。
⟦{部屋|へや}→部屋：00507_heya⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{窓|まど}→窓：02254_mado⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{四|よっ}→四：noentry⟧つ⟦あります→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There are four windows in the room.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{菓子|かし}→お菓子：02852_okashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{八|やっ}→八：noentry⟧つ⟦ありました→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{五|いつ}→五：noentry⟧つ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦あげました→あげる：00546_ageru⟧。⟦{三|みっ}→三：noentry⟧つ⟦{残|のこ}りました→残る：01187_nokoru⟧。
examples.english: There were eight sweets, but I gave five to the children. Three remained.

notes:
つ is the most versatile Japanese counter. It uses native Japanese (やまとことば) numbers and can count almost anything when you don't know the specific counter. It only works for numbers 1-9.

COUNTING FORMS:
- ⟦{一|ひと}→一：noentry⟧つ (1), ⟦{二|ふた}→二：noentry⟧つ (2), ⟦{三|みっ}→三：noentry⟧つ (3)
- ⟦{四|よっ}→四：noentry⟧つ (4), ⟦{五|いつ}→五：noentry⟧つ (5), ⟦{六|むっ}→六：noentry⟧つ (6)
- ⟦{七|なな}→七：00734_nana⟧つ (7), ⟦{八|やっ}→八：noentry⟧つ (8), ⟦{九|ここの}→九：noentry⟧つ (9)

LIMITATIONS:
- No form for 10 or above. For 10, use ⟦{十|とお}→十：00708_juu⟧. For higher numbers, use specific counters or the Chinese-derived number system.
- Cannot count people (use ⟦{人|にん}→〜人：00658_nin⟧) or long thin objects (use ⟦{本|ほん}→〜本：00688_hon⟧).

USAGE:
This is the safest counter to use when unsure which specific counter applies. It sounds natural for small objects, abstract things, and items on a list.
